newsitem.title: CROATIA: Tudjman takes early lead in Croatian election.
newsitem.headline: Tudjman takes early lead in Croatian election.

text.p: Croatian President Franjo Tudjman looked set for victory in a presidential election with around two thirds of the votes counted, preliminary results broadcast on Croatian television showed on Monday.

First partial results showed Tudjman had won 59 percent, far ahead of both opposition candidates. He is now virtually assured of winning outright in the first round without the need for a run-off against an opposition candidate.
"I expect full results to be even better," Tudjman said after the results from some 57 percent of votes were announced. "The rivals got as much as they promised to people in their programmes."

"I promise the continuity of the policy with which we established Croatian freedom and independence, a stable economy and currency...We are leaving behind the state of war, now we shall dedicate ourselves with all our forces to raising the standards of living for the entire population," he told reporters.
Zdravko Tomac of the Social Democratic party was in second place with 22.8 percent of the votes counted and Vlado Gotovac of the Croatian Social Liberal Party was third with 18.1 percent.

The 75-year-old former general is now in a position to lead Croatia into the 21st century. But he has been reported to be suffering from cancer. Unnamed U.S. officials said in November he had been treated for a form of stomach cancer in Washington.

He is likely to come under increasing pressure from the United States and the West to tighten up his record on treatment of Serbs in Croatia and to loosen his grip on the state media if he is to fulfil Croatia's dream of joining Western institutions.

At a party thrown for his Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) supporters on Sunday night Tudjman clapped along to chants of "Franjo, Franjo" as supporters crowded round him, waving flags and singing. Fireworks lit up the sky after the first results were announced.
The atmosphere at both opposition headquarters was far more subdued than at Tudjman's celebration.

"There is no food or drink here but the results are above what we expected, especially in the cities. We had a modest campaign but I am sure we'll fare even better in the next election and we'll eventually build a modern democratic Croatia," Tomac told reporters.
Both opposition candidates have already branded the election campaign undemocratic and biased, highlighting Tudjman's control of the state media.

"At this moment we failed to incite the feeling that elections matter. A large number of people did not turn out and I think they might have voted for us, because HDZ supporters duly cast their ballots," said Gotovac.

Head of the state electoral commission Ivan Mrkonjic told reporters votes from 5,247 polling stations out of a total of 7,558 had been counted, or around 57 percent. Votes from soldiers, prisoners and sailors have still to be included.
Tudjman has been hailed as the "father of the nation" since he proclaimed independence for Croatia after its secession from federal Yugoslavia in 1991.
